categories.name: Resolve via timely payment
categories.description: Resolution of the fine case through early or timely payment made by the offender. This activity maximizes timely fine revenue (Make +100) and helps minimize administrative and enforcement costs (Help +50), as measured by the average time to case closure indicator (id=114).
categories.rationale: Maps 1:1 to the declared alternative id=12 from the goal model. Supported by frequent narrative variants such as V0002, V0003, V0004, and V0007 where payment occurs shortly after fine creation or sending.

categories.name: Resolve via delinquent payment
categories.description: Resolution of the fine case through payment occurring after penalties or enforcement steps have been initiated. This alternative helps maximize timely fine revenue (Help +50) and is evaluated against the average time to case closure indicator (id=114).
categories.rationale: Maps 1:1 to the declared alternative id=13. Supported by narrative variants such as V0005, V0006, and V0009 where payments are observed after notification and penalty additions.

categories.name: Resolve via administrative appeal to the Prefecture
categories.description: Resolution of the case through an administrative appeal submitted to the Prefecture. This alternative preserves the offender's due-process rights (Help +50), but negatively impacts administrative costs (SomeNegative -25) and fine revenue (SomeNegative -25). It is measured by the time to appeal filing, Prefecture indicator (id=113).
categories.rationale: Maps 1:1 to the declared alternative id=14. Sub-steps include inserting the appeal date, sending the appeal, receiving the result, and notifying the offender, as observed in variants like V0008, V0057, and V0135.

categories.name: Resolve via judicial appeal to the Judge
categories.description: Resolution of the case through a judicial appeal brought before a Judge. This option strongly makes preservation of due-process rights (Make +100), but hurts minimization of administrative costs (Hurt -50) and fine revenue (SomeNegative -25). It is tracked via the time to appeal filing, Judge indicator (id=175).
categories.rationale: Maps 1:1 to the declared alternative id=19. Evidence in the sample includes variants such as V0103, V0176, and V0224 where judicial appeals are logged.

categories.name: Resolve via coercive credit collection
categories.description: Resolution of the case through coercive credit collection measures after standard enforcement processes fail. This path helps maximize fine revenue (Help +50) but hurts administrative and enforcement cost minimization (Hurt -50) and due-process preservation (SomeNegative -25). Evaluated using the average time to case closure indicator (id=114).
categories.rationale: Maps 1:1 to the declared alternative id=20. Observed in high-duration variants such as V0001, V0134, and V0138 where cases culminate in sending for credit collection.
